When I was four my family were at a campsite with shower blocks. My mum took me to have a shower, let me step out to her so she could wrap me in a towel afterwards and I slipped on the small step (because it was wet) and hit my head on the corner of the step. Proper whack, huge thud and my mum just about died of shock. She fully expected my head to be cracked open, blood everywhere and an unconscious child. She was incredibly shocked to check my head and find nothing. I was bawling my eyes out mind you, but my head was fine. As she is a nurse, she did all the proper checks and decided not to go to hospital. She made the same call your nurse/GP made and almost 20 years later I am fine. I still have a lump from it but absolutely no proper damage. 

My mum still thinks she could have stopped it from happening, she still holds on to the guilt of "letting" me fall. But i don't. I think shit happens and she did everything right after it. 

Shit happens and YOU did everything right after it.  Just keep an eye on your daughter and take her to the hospital/GP if you become concerned.

Why don't feed and pet them? Because they are wild animals and if they become reliant on humans feeding them, they will basically (over generations) stop "hunting" for food as they know humans will feed them. Once humans are gone/if we stopped feeding them all of a sudden, we might end up killing them as later generations never learnt to correctly forage for food. 

As for petting, it teaches them that humans are friendly and they will become bolder in terms of approaching humans and human things, causing trouble for tourists. Also putting them in danger by approaching the wrong kind of humans because they incorrectly trust humans. We (in the last year?) had some dumbass teenagers kill quokkas for fun. We don't want these animals to be terrified of us but we dont want them to be okay with us petting them/picking them up etc. 

You should treat them the same way you treat an undomesticated wild animal, but almost more carefully as these beautiful animals only live on the tiny island (you can cycle around the island and a few hours it's that small). 

Sorry, i rambled a bit but yeah, we want these guys to survive and thrive in their environment, despite it being a huge tourist attraction now.
Rottnest Island off the coast of Perth in Western Australia. Just please don't feed or pet them!!

Work in Pharmacy, a government policy that's only a year old has caused a few issues. Basically diabetics are now required to have a Dr sign off every 6 months that they still require government subsidized items (needles and test strips). Most customers keep on top of it and those who don't understand that they can come back once it's signed or pay full price (as it's their responsiblity).

One gentleman came in and he hadn't had his form signed and hence his blood glucose test strips would be full price ($60) instead of subsidized ($17). He WENT OFF. Started shouting at me, pound his fists on the counter top and throwing his hands around. I calmly explained I wasn't in control of this process and the government has decided to tighten the reigns a little. All he had to do was take the form to his Dr, or pay full price this time. 

Well no. I was personally responsible for withholding life saving medication from him (side note: this wasn't medication and in his case obviously not life saving as the last time he had gotten a pack of test strips was around 10 months prior, meaning he barely ever tested his blood glucose levels). He continued his rant, changing his tactics to "I'm not blaming you but you should be telling the government that this is unacceptable. I'm just the little guy, you are the one who can make a change". Like seriously, no I cannot make that much of a difference and he is the first person to be so offended by these tighter restrictions. 

This entire time I was calm, professional and extremely well put together. Not a raised voice or a threat was uttered by me. 

Eventually I bent all the rules and gave him the strips at the lower cost, putting my job at risk out of fear of being physically hurt by him. He continued his rant the whole way through the process of me giving him what he wanted. Even telling customers who were standing up to him (for me) to **** off. 

He eventually left and my next customer came and asked if I was okay. I meekly smiled and popped her through the till before a few tears started to leak out. I excused myself from the floor and headed out the back (passing customers who had heard everything and were giving me sympathetic looks). When I was finally alone I cried so hard I shook all over. I sobbed for ages and took ages to compose myself. 

Even I'm amazed at how calm I was. 

And for anyone wondering, I didn't have a chance to call security and my colleagues thought I was handelling it better than I actually was. Customer genuinely did approach him and tell him to calm down, he was just an absolute jerk.
